question: Iron-deficient children are at risk of developing pica; if they then ingest soil or paint containing lead, the resulting iron deficiency further enhances lead absorption, creating a vicious cycle of pica, worsening iron deficiency, and lead poisoning.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. The pica-iron deficiency-lead poisoning triad is a well-recognised vicious cycle: iron deficiency promotes pica; pica introduces lead through soil or paint ingestion; iron deficiency amplifies lead absorption; and lead impairs haematopoiesis, deepening iron deficiency. Correcting iron status is central to breaking this cycle.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. This bidirectional relationship is a critical clinical concept. Iron deficiency drives pica; pica (soil, paint) exposes children to lead; iron deficiency independently increases gastrointestinal lead absorption; and lead toxicity itself impairs haem synthesis, further deepening iron-deficiency anaemia. Treating the iron deficiency is therefore a priority in managing pica.
